facts.text: Saratoga Springs grew around hot springs near the Jordan River, where settlers opened Beck's Saratoga Springs resort in 1884, named after the New York original.
The town incorporated on December 31 1997, became a city in 2001, and has expanded rapidly along Utah Lake’s northwestern shore.
In 2010 the council seeded a library with $10,000, and by 2013 it had grown enough to warrant full‑time staff, a rare municipal library model.
Because Utah County’s land‑development rules were too rural, landowners pushed for incorporation to preserve the resort‑style character of the area.
A Church of Jesus Christ of Latter‑Day Saints temple was announced for Saratoga Springs in 2008 and dedicated on August 13 2023 after an open house from April to July.
The Knolls Fire on June 28 2020 forced evacuation of roughly 13,000 people in 3,100 homes across Saratoga Springs.
